correctness.rationale: For an equilateral triangle the source one-vertex inequality at A reduces exactly to \(R_A\ge r_b+r_c\). The identity \((|u+v|+|u-v|)/2=\max(|u|,|v|)\) turns the inward corner into two linear half-planes. Rotating them gives six half-planes; exact pairwise intersections yield the displayed six vertices, and exact shoelace arithmetic gives \(\frac45(3\sqrt2-\sqrt3)\). The bundled verifier replays these identities in \(\mathbb Q(\sqrt2,\sqrt3)\).

value.rationale: The source itself asks an area question for the curve-bounded Erdős–Mordell extension and singles out the equilateral case. The canonical polygon M is the paper’s rigorous, construction-level guaranteed subset of that region. Its exact area is therefore a natural motivated invariant, not an arbitrary slice: it supplies a closed-form analytic benchmark and a rigorous equilateral area enlargement of \(\frac{4\sqrt6-9}{5}\) using only the source’s three local inequalities. The result does not pretend to solve the full E' area problem.
